newsitem.title: VATICAN: African bishops blame politics for ethnic strife.
newsitem.headline: African bishops blame politics for ethnic strife.

text.p: African Catholic bishops have said a political power struggle fuelled the ethnic hate that has led to rampant violence in the Great Lakes region.
In a document released by the Vatican on Monday, bishops from Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda blamed "the struggle for internal and external political alliances" for the strife in their region.
"The diversity of ethnicities constitutes a wealth for any country," said the document, signed by the bishops on Saturday following a three-day meeting in Nairobi.
"But ethnic diversity becomes the worst threat when private or political interests transform it into ideology and a tool of conquest and power," the document said.
"Ethnocentric ideology, through the squalid trafficking of arms, generates conflicts and fuels a spiral of discrimination, exclusion and violence that extends to massacre and genocide," it added.
The Great Lakes area has been hard hit by ethnic violence.

Up to one million people were slaughtered in Rwanda during ethnic violence in 1994 which sparked the exodus of more than two million refugees to Zaire and Tanzania, many of whom are only now beginning to return to their native lands.
Medical workers said on Sunday that thousands may die if no food is distributed in the next few days to Rwandan refugees trapped in the remote Zaire village of Tingi-Tingi.
